task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of May 22, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: The Department of Energy awarded a $14.2 billion offshore wind development contract to Horizon Marine Energy on May 22, 2025.
The contract is the largest single renewable energy development award in U.S. history, according to the department.
The Horizon installation will be located 80 kilometers off the Cape Hartley coast and will consist of 280 turbines with a combined nameplate capacity of 4,200 megawatts.
Each turbine is rated at 15 megawatts, a class that is not yet in commercial deployment and is scheduled to enter production in 2026.
Energy Secretary Isabel Makin said: "This contract moves the United States from a follower to a leader in offshore wind. At full output, it will power more than 1.8 million homes."
Horizon CEO Peter Strand said the company expects to begin offshore foundation installation in early 2027 and deliver first power to the grid by mid-2029.
The project will require an undersea high-voltage direct current cable of 92 kilometers to connect the offshore substation to the mainland grid.
Independent analysts note that offshore wind capacity factors typically range from 40% to 55%; at the low end, the array would average approximately 1,680 megawatts of actual generation.

Three commercial fishing associations expressed concern about the siting, saying portions of the cable route cross productive lobster grounds; they called for an independent impact assessment before construction.
The contract requires Horizon to meet domestic content requirements for at least 50% of major components, a threshold that will require substantial new manufacturing in the U.S.
Horizon has a partnership with Strandvik Turbine Systems, a Norwegian manufacturer, to build the 15-megawatt turbines at a new plant in Portview, Maine.
The department estimates the project will support 7,400 construction jobs and 600 permanent operations positions at peak activity.
Cape Hartley is in a wind resource area classified as Excellent by NOAA, with average offshore wind speeds of 9.2 meters per second at hub height.
Environmental regulators approved the project area under the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act after a three-year environmental review.
Horizon will pay the federal government $420 million in annual lease fees once the array is operational.
The state legislature in the coastal state passed a complementary grid integration bill in April 2025 requiring utilities to build additional onshore transmission to accommodate the new generation.
The U.S. has 3,800 megawatts of offshore wind operating as of May 2025, all on smaller arrays built along the Northeast coast.
The 15-megawatt turbine class requires installation vessels larger than any currently operating in U.S. waters; Horizon has contracted for two purpose-built vessels from a shipyard in Gulfport.
Strand said Horizon has $6.1 billion in committed financing and is seeking the remainder through a federal loan guarantee program.
The contract includes financial penalties if the project does not deliver commercial power by December 2030.

forbidden_additions: a claim that the project is already generating power
a confirmed fish catch decline attributed to the wind farm
a total cost figure different from $14.2 billion
